rules: One task per session. Split before implementation if one observable contract cannot fit a small change.
Files are starting points; new: marks a planned file, not an existing artifact.
Validation commands for new files are acceptance commands, not claims of current success.
A dependency must be done with evidence, not merely implemented or claimed.
Backend-policy decisions and operational evidence require the approvals described in the session guide.
Add exact source, commands, results, artifacts and limitations to evidence before marking done.

KL09 optimization cards carry an outcome-branch criterion: accepted (all criteria met) or a measured rejection with reverted code; both are done and must record evidence.disposition (docs/plan/performance-leadership.md section 6).
A dependency listed in requires_accepted is satisfied only when that card is done with disposition accepted.
At most one in_progress card per hot file across all lanes; claims record write_set and are made atomic by pushing to origin/main (docs/plan/performance-leadership.md section 7).

evidence.results: rec_bytes now reserves key, value, and header key/value lengths. A zero-length record cannot bypass a saturated buffer. Header-heavy records are rejected at the cap. evidence.results: Transaction-partition, encode, and injected write failures before an in-flight registration release the buffer permit once, roll back uncommitted sequences, fail the accepted futures, and make flush observe the failure. tasks.title: Make worker shutdown and clone races bounded
tasks.deliverable: A tested terminal lifecycle for close, close_timeout, last-handle drop and concurrent sends.
acceptance: Do not regress the existing durable Closed flag across clones.
Stalled brokers/retry queues cannot leave completions or owned tasks alive indefinitely after the declared shutdown outcome.

evidence.results: close_timeout against a stalled broker returns Timeout within the deadline. An in-flight record completes with Timeout, which is ambiguous delivery, not proof it was never written. Concurrent sends after close see Closed on every clone. Dropping the last handle aborts workers and releases buffer permits. The durable Closed flag is unchanged.
limits: Timeout after transmission is still not a broker-confirmed ambiguous receipt. It only refuses to claim non-delivery.

acceptance: Each retry consumes remaining time rather than restarting a full delivery budget.

commands: cargo test --offline --locked --test full_surface timeout (3 passed, exit 0)

evidence.results: A record's delivery deadline is reused across metadata refresh, retry backoff, write, and acknowledgment wait. Retries do not restart a full delivery budget. max_block still bounds enqueue admission separately from request_timeout. A timed-out transmitted record completes as Timeout, not as proof of non-delivery.
limits: Timeout after transmission is still not a broker-confirmed ambiguous receipt.

tasks.title: Use an absolute deadline for a network round trip
tasks.deliverable: A shared remaining-time contract for request write, header/body read and partial-frame progress.
acceptance: A peer that delays both write and response cannot consume two independent full RPC budgets.
Partial reads, wakeup/cancellation and TLS read-during-write preserve framing and correlation safety.
No timeout returns a reusable desynchronized connection.
validation: cargo test --locked --test network_deadlines
cargo test --locked --lib net

evidence.results: BrokerConn::roundtrip shares one absolute deadline across write and read. A peer that delays both cannot consume two full budgets. Timeout, cancellation, partial read, and correlation mismatch mark the connection closed so it is not reused. Framing is preserved when a response arrives during write.
limits: Producer::fire still calls write_all_timeout and read_response separately, so that path can still spend two request_timeout budgets. Callers of BrokerConn::roundtrip, including consumer fetch and coordinator RPCs, share one deadline.

tasks.title: Bound consumer fetch buffering across brokers
tasks.deliverable: A bounded aggregate fetch/decode/pending-record policy, not only per-request max_bytes.
acceptance: Slow processing and max_poll_records do not permit unbounded prefetched memory across partitions/brokers.
Preserve progress for a valid first batch larger than the soft fetch limit, with an explicit hard decode ceiling.
Pause/resume/seek/drop release or retain buffers according to the ownership contract without committing undelivered data.
validation: cargo test --locked --test fetch_buffer_budget
cargo test --locked --test consumer_fetch_semantics

evidence.results: ConsumerConfig::buffer_memory defaults to 32 MiB and bounds retained prefetch bytes (key, value, and headers) across partitions and brokers. Zero disables the cap. A valid first batch larger than the soft fetch limit is accepted so the partition can make progress, up to the existing 64 MiB decode ceiling. Pause retains those bytes, seek and clear release them, and position stays the delivered offset.
limits: Process RSS is not bounded. A single Fetch response is fully decoded before the retention check, and one round may request every leader before later responses are discarded. The 64 MiB decode ceiling is unchanged.

Caller-selected Codec resolves writer/reader schemas once and retains immutable selections; defaults, unions, named references, promotions and compatibility are explicit codec responsibilities.
Encoding obtains exact writer-schema datum length, checks overflow/frame limit before allocation, reserves one bounded frame fallibly, and supplies only its exact payload slice.

evidence.hypothesis: BrokerConn::write_request_deadline splits its BytesMut after each RPC, assumed to hand off capacity and trigger fresh per-RPC request allocations. Reusing the whole request buffer was expected to reduce allocations per RPC.
evidence.finding: The hypothesis does not hold with the locked bytes 1.12.1. BytesMut::split leaves the spare-capacity view in BrokerConn; after the completed payload is dropped, reserve reclaims the original backing allocation. A 10,000-request census records one 40-byte shared-allocation metadata promotion, with zero subsequent per-RPC allocations at all sizes through 16 KiB. A 64 KiB request additionally requires one growth allocation in both arms. Named producer data requests already use Worker.write_buf and BrokerConn::write_all_timeout rather than the targeted request encoder.

evidence.hypothesis: Sequential BrokerConn::connect_tls_any waits for an unreachable first bootstrap address to exhaust its TCP connect timeout before trying a reachable second address. The candidate reduced stalled-first construction-to-first-ack latency by 66.6196% at the median paired point (95% CI -67.5603% to -66.2511%).
